name: The Tapestry Solar
summary: The lord's private room: a sloped writing desk under a shelf of books, a high-backed settle by the fire, a livery cupboard, and two verdure tapestries.
description: Above the noise of the hall the lord keeps a room of his own. He writes at a sloped oak desk under a shelf of books that he has mostly read, and when he stops he sits in a high-backed settle with its back to the draught and its front to the fire. Two verdure tapestries warm the walls, green wool thick enough to stop a draught and valuable enough to be rolled up and carried out when the household moves. The livery cupboard holds the evening's wine and a pewter flagon; the iron-bound chest under the south tapestry holds the letters he would rather nobody read.
